summary: The whole workflow works. The list page filter is a GET form: typing does not filter live, but Enter or the Search button navigates to ?q=Hmong / ?q=Karen and shows "1 matching brief" with only the matching community, a "Clear search" link, and a proper empty state for a non-match ("0 matching briefs / No community matched that name..."); matching is case-insensitive and partial (?q=hmo, ?q=deaf). On /minnesota-communities/hmong, "Community brief" and "Learning and reflection" are aria-pressed tab toggles that swap the content panel (brief sections vs three lessons with "In this lesson" / "Consider this situation"); "Explore the reasoning" only exists inside the Learning panel (3 per page), toggles aria-expanded false->true, relabels to "Close the reflection" and unhides a community-specific reasoning paragraph; "Save resource" becomes "Saved to My work" (aria-pressed true) with a live-region message "Saved to My work on this device." Saving made no /api call: it writes localStorage key one-dsd-saved-resources-v1 ({version:1, items:[{href,title,savedAt}]}). /my-work lists the saved brief under "Saved resources" with a Remove button (aria-label "Remove Hmong Minnesota from saved resources"); it survives reload, the link navigates back to the brief (which still shows Saved), Remove empties it and that also persists; a fresh browser context shows no saved items, confirming per-browser storage, not server-side. Deaf/DeafBlind/hard of hearing and Rural pages have the same four controls and behave identically, with their own scenarios and reasoning text. All six "Download this brief" endpoints return 200 with correct content types and attachment filenames. No console errors, no responses >= 400, no 4xx/5xx on any page. Only read-only GETs were made; no form was submitted other than the GET search box.

summary: The /start page holds a three-question orientation form (role select, area-of-work select, four urgency radios, submit button "Show me a place to start"). It is purely client-side: filling it as a new staff member (Staff member / Culture, trust, and repair / I'm planning ahead) and submitting produced, without navigation and without any API call, a tailored recommendation panel ("Start with Culture, trust, and repair." with an urgency-specific paragraph, three "Work you can begin now" bullets and three links: Explore this area -> /areas#culture_trust_repair, Open a guided practice -> /practice, Find the right person -> /support/right-person?area=culture_trust_repair). All links returned 200 and the right-person page honoured the area parameter with a "Back to culture, trust, and repair" link. Four other role/area/urgency combinations each produced a distinct, correct recommendation. Validation works: submitting empty or partial shows per-field red role="alert" messages, sets aria-invalid and moves focus to the first missing field. As the page itself states ("Your answers stay on this page; they are not saved"), nothing is written to localStorage, sessionStorage or cookies, so the choices do not survive a reload and /home and /learn show no personalised content. The only /api call on every page is GET /api/page-text?route=... (200). No console errors, no responses >= 400, no horizontal scroll at 375px. No problems found that block or mislead a user.

summary: The home page, header navigation (desktop and mobile menu), the two-input "Show me" form on /home, the free-text library search and the root welcome page all work. Caveat on the brief: the two-input form on /home is a role/task navigator made of two <select>s (no text box), so "interpreter"/"waiver" cannot be typed there; keyword search lives at /library (linked from /home as "Resource library"), where it is a plain GET form (/library?q=...) rendered server-side with no search API call. "interpreter" returned 193 results with relevant top hits, "waiver" 160, an empty search simply shows the full library (765 resources), and "zzqqxx" shows a clear "No closely related resource found" message with recovery links. All 24 top result links open real pages. The only /api traffic is GET /api/page-text?route=... (a read-aloud/"Listen" helper), always 200 when it completed. Zero console errors, zero 4xx/5xx and zero page errors across the main runs; the one 404 observed was a read-aloud JSON file on a legacy static self-directed course page reached from a "waiver" result. No login or secrets encountered. No forms that create records were submitted and /api/ask was never called. Two low-severity issues: that 404, and the header logo (labelled "...home") sending visitors back to the splash gate "/" instead of /home. Note: my first script run falsely suggested pages were stuck on "Opening your page..."; a dedicated probe proved that was a measurement artifact (client-side transitions finish in 0.3-2.2 s).

summary: The Learn hub, its four filter controls (search, theme, level, format), the theme page, browse=all, /courses, /learn/paths, course detail pages, lesson pages and the self-directed course viewer all load and behave correctly; filtering changes result counts as expected and selections survive the GET round-trip. Progress is browser-local only (localStorage): the self-directed viewer saves the page you are on (one-dsd-learning-F02 = {page, visitedAt}) and restores it after reload; /courses lessons save answers under pac-course:* keys and restore them after reload. The suspected read-aloud defect is confirmed: every course page requests /learning/geffen-read-aloud/courses/<course>.json and gets a 404 (self-directed-F02, self-directed-F01, F05, I01, A01, F24, anti-racism-resource, disability-and-language all 404), so the "Listen through the page" panel stays hidden and there is no read-aloud control a user can press on any course page. The page falls back silently to text (no visible error), so this is medium rather than high. No /api/ calls other than GET /api/page-text (all 200). No forms were submitted and POST /api/ask was not called.

summary: The "Find the right person" helper at /support/right-person works end to end. It is a client-side form (3 selects: role, area of work, timing; plus a 3-option radio "Is the work within DSD?"; no free-text field, so nothing is sent to the server). Submitting with blanks shows inline validation messages via aria-live ("Choose the role closest to your work.", "Choose the area closest to your task.", "Choose when you need to act."). Three complete walkthroughs each produced a sensible, complete recommendation panel: a headline ("Find support for DSD work" when DSD is self-attested, "Connect with the right person" otherwise), a timing-specific "Begin with the work" next step with two buttons (Review this area -> /areas#<area>, Find material -> /library?q=<area>), and a "People and offices to consider" list naming roles/offices (e.g. "The responsible accessibility or language access lead", "Human Resources", "The appropriate civil-rights channel", "Your administration Equity Director", "An Equity Specialist supporting your area", "The responsible policy or program owner") with supporting mn.gov guidance links and a closing link to /support/directory. Recommendations vary correctly with inputs (language-access scenario added the access lead + civil-rights channel; policy scenario added the policy/program owner; HR/outside-DSD scenario led with Human Resources). The /areas anchors referenced by "Review this area" exist, and /library?q= and /support/directory render. No /api call is made on submit; the only /api traffic is GET /api/page-text?route=... (200) on page load. No console errors, no page errors, no responses >= 400. Answers and results are NOT persisted: after a reload the form resets and the result panel returns to its placeholder; localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies are all empty. All 24 unique links on /support (and the internal result links) returned 200. Of 7 external mn.gov links in results, 5 returned 200 via curl; 2 (DHS accessibility page and civil-rights-in-human-services page) redirected curl to a ShieldSquare/perfdrive bot-check and the headless browser could not resolve mn.gov in this sandbox, so those two could not be confirmed from here (likely bot protection, not a broken link). Two low-severity notes only; no blocking issues found.
